results.summary: This is a test structure for a flip-flop implemented in the SKY130 process, intended for analog characterization. It is not designed for the standard demo board but requires a dedicated test platform with FPGA hardware to drive control signals with precise timing. The documentation is minimal, stating only that design data should be consulted and that no test procedure has been written yet. The exact testing platform is still to be determined.

This project contains test structures for a future register file macro, implemented in the SKY130 process. It is not intended for the standard demo board but requires a dedicated test platform with FPGA hardware to drive control signals with precise timing. The documentation is minimal, stating only that design data should be consulted and that no test procedure has been written yet. The exact testing platform is still to be determined.

This design is a demo entry for the TT08 demo competition, implemented in Verilog. It outputs VGA video and audio signals, using the Tiny VGA and TT Audio pinouts. To use it, a TinyVGA Pmod and an audio Pmod are required on the demo board. The documentation is incomplete, with a TODO for the 'How it works' section, but the test procedure is described.

AICD Playground is a mixed-signal test project for the analog IC design course at Graz University of Technology. It integrates a digital 8-bit controller with analog IPs including level shifters, an R2R DAC, and a comparator, forming a simple SAR-ADC. The design is configured via SPI to load memory with a program, and then the CPU executes it to perform analog-to-digital conversion. No external hardware is necessary for basic operation.

This is a RISC-V SoC based on TinyQV, implementing the RV32EC instruction set with additional extensions. It uses QSPI flash for program storage and QSPI PSRAM for data memory, and includes peripherals such as UART, SPI, and PWM. The design is intended to be used with a QSPI Pmod containing flash and RAM, and can drive an ST7789 LCD display via SPI. Testing requires loading an image into flash and following a specific reset sequence, typically handled by MicroPython scripts on the demo board's RP2040.

This design is a test circuit for DDR throughput and flip-flop aperture, implemented in Verilog. It generates a 2x clock by detecting edges on the input clock and its complement, with varying pulse widths controlled by inverter chains. The outputs capture data on these pulses and on a normal flip-flop, allowing comparison. Testing requires an Analog Discovery 3 or similar equipment to drive and observe the signals.

Padlock is a digital lock design implemented in Wokwi that stores a 7-bit secret code and indicates locked or unlocked status on a 7-segment display. The user sets the code via input pins and toggles a set pin to store it; entering the correct code unlocks the safe until reset. The design is tested by setting the clock to free-running mode and following a sequence of input changes. No external hardware is required.

This project implements a true random number generator using three ring oscillators of different lengths (6, 12, and 24 inverters) whose outputs are XORed to produce a chaotic bitstream. A Von Neumann corrector debiases the stream, and 32-bit random numbers are output via UART at 9600 baud. The raw oscillator outputs are also available on pins for monitoring. A UART-to-USB adapter is required to view the generated numbers.

This is an 8-bit direct digital synthesizer (DDS) that generates a digitized sine wave with user-defined frequency. The frequency is set by an 8-bit phase increment loaded via input pins, and the output is an 8-bit amplitude sample updated every clock cycle. An external R-2R ladder DAC is required to convert the digital output to an analog sine wave. The design is based on standard DDS principles and can produce frequencies up to about 33 MHz at a 66 MHz clock.

This project implements a hardware-optimized Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LIF) neuron in Verilog, designed for area efficiency while maintaining biological realism. It includes a serial interface for loading parameters and provides outputs for membrane voltage and spike events. The design can be used with DIP switches for stimulus and LEDs or a 7-segment display for monitoring. No external hardware is required for basic operation.
